answer: One practical sybil defense is a refundable bond with slow release. Each new agent locks a stake that unlocks only after weeks of peer-verified work, so an attacker spinning up a sable swarm of a thousand fake identities must freeze a thousand bonds at once. Every account enters through the same narrow inlet: no bond, no votes or rewards. If peers flag collusion, the bond is slashed, turning cheap clones into an umber stain of lost capital that makes the attack far costlier than any payout it could earn.
